extraction.name: MATH Dataset
extraction.description: A dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems with step-by-step solutions, along with a large auxiliary pretraining dataset (AMPS) to teach models the fundamentals of mathematics.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Bums, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The MATH dataset problems were collected from mathematics competitions via aops.com. The AMPS pretraining dataset was collected from Khan Academy exercises and generated using manually designed Mathematica scripts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Problems from high school math competitions (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME), Khan Academy exercises, and algorithmically generated problems using Mathematica's computer algebra system.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Problems and solutions were consistently formatted using LATEX and the Asymptote vector graphics language. Final boxed answers were forced to follow consistent formatting rules (e.g., probabilities as simplified fractions, specific fraction and parenthesis encodings) to allow for automatic assessment using exact match.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each problem includes a step-by-step solution and a final boxed answer. The final answers are wrapped and delimited with the \boxed{} command to allow for automatic evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset could potentially be used to train models that help students cheat on mathematics exams, though the authors explicitly state this is not the intended use.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is unusually challenging for current models, and accuracy increases only modestly with model size, indicating that simply scaling up Transformers will not solve the task.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking mathematical problem-solving ability, pretraining models on mathematics fundamentals, and forecasting reasoning capabilities.

name.evidence: To measure the problem-solving ability of machine leaming models, we introduce the MATH dataset, which consists of 12;500problems from high school math competitions.

description.evidence: To measure this ability in machine leaming models, we introduce MATH, a new dataset of 12;500 challenging competition mathematics problems. Each problem in MATH has a full step-by-step solution... we also contribute a large auxiliary pretraining dataset which helps teach models the fundamentals of mathematics.
